report:
Reviewed the complete source_evidence claim, three ordinary implementation associations, and the one associated TODO test. Requirements are (1) semantic integration inputs are Rust source in a checked-in Cargo sample, (2) execution traverses the production workspace host, live provider, actor, and Axum server, (3) snapshots observe returned values and demand, and (4) expected JSON/scripted semantic providers never supply semantic results. The architectural-foundations rationale preserves focused constructed-value/unit boundary tests without treating them as end-to-end semantic evidence.

The inspector_project helper resolves test-projects/semantic-inspector/db-drop-guard; the captured manifest is a real 2024-edition Cargo library and its captured lib.rs defines Db, DbDropGuard and db() calling clone. The ordinary run_inspector association opens SageHost::try_open from the process working directory, constructs LiveInspectionProvider over that host, sends requests through InspectionClient/serve_actor on the database actor thread, then passes the client to run_server. The ordinary server association uses axum::serve with production routes; handlers call the typed client and serialize responses. The captured actor dispatch directly invokes provider.symbols, symbol, product, and run while recording demand. Essential command and server entry-point associations were added as comments before this fresh review so their source is now checked for freshness.

The supplied semantic_inspector.rs is integration evidence infrastructure, including real_symbol_index_is_complete_local_and_detail_free, live-source edit scenarios, and real_command_serves_embedded_assets_and_correlated_request_logs. The latter launches the real compiled cargo-sage executable in the checked-in project, requests production HTTP routes, obtains symbol paths and run IDs from live responses, asserts protocol/root/selected-symbol/product/run values, and snapshots actual response bodies and the twelve request events parsed from process stderr. Its visible summary and demand snapshot are assembled from those returned values, never read as an API response. Other source-driven tests snapshot reflected value shapes and assert cold/warm demand properties; the edit matrix changes Rust text through FileUpdate and asserts changed versus unchanged returned values. Synthetic Salsa probes elsewhere in the supplied file test instrumentation lifecycle only and are not offered as replacement semantic integration inputs.

The only formally associated test is sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_inspector_inspection_source_evidence. It has no assertions and remains explicitly TODO. Its comment identifies the prerequisite: associate and review complete backend and browser scenarios launching the real command on the sample, observing values/UI/demand, and demonstrating source edits through the live database. Existing backend source and the successful HTTP smoke scenario provide partial substantive support, but do not complete that browser/association prerequisite. I accept that explicit deferral rather than counting the placeholder as a passing behavioral test. No N/A entries exist. All claim aspects are accounted for by the source-input/execution wiring and explicitly deferred complete integration evidence; no contradictory snapshot-as-input path was found in the reviewed evidence.

Executed cargo fmt, cargo build (success, existing compiler warnings), and cargo test --test semantic_inspector real_command_serves_embedded_assets_and_correlated_request_logs -- --exact (one passed, nine filtered). Other test descriptions above are source inspection, not execution claims. Review start/read captured the fixture, rationale, review specification, and actor dependency; record checks their freshness. Central post-codegen and Sage sanity reviews remain the coordinator's responsibility for the two comment-only association additions.
